decisive_spans.text: swelling of her right upper eyelid, which had discharged pus for the previous 10 months without any trauma to her head

response.rationale: The vignette describes chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge, which is highly consistent with chronic dacryocystitis. While pyogenic granuloma is supported by the description of a 'scarlike node discharging pus', the chronicity and specific location of the swelling point more strongly to dacryocystitis. Orbital cellulitis is contradicted by the absence of orbital or intracranial lesions and lack of fever.
